role: Federal regulatory agency — setting maximum methylmercury limit for fish
stance_basis: referenced solely as the regulatory standard-setter for the 0.5 ug/g methylmercury limit in fish
summary: The FDA is mentioned only as the source of the 0.5 ug/g maximum methylmercury limit for edible portions of fish, against which mercury levels in Lake Jocassee largemouth bass and other species are compared. The agency does not express a position on the project itself; it is cited purely as a regulatory benchmark. No complaint or opposition to the project is attributed to the FDA.
summary_quote: Sherer (1975) and Abernathy (1975) have reported mercury levels in largemouth bass (Micropterus salmoides) that are above the maximum methylmercury limit for edible portions of fish of 0.5 ug/g set by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA).
